questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: In sponges, water enters through minute pores (ostia) in the body wall into a central cavity, the spongocoel. From the spongocoel, the water goes out through the:

solution.explanation: NCERT: sponges have a water transport or canal system. Water enters through minute pores (ostia) in the body wall into a central cavity, the spongocoel, from where it goes out through the osculum.
solution.why_others_wrong: The hypostome bears the mouth of coelenterates; the excretory pore belongs to aschelminths; a cloaca is a common chamber found in vertebrates such as amphibians, reptiles and birds.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Animal Kingdom', phylum Porifera
solution.final_answer: Option A: Osculum

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Among cartilaginous fishes, some possess electric organs while some possess a poison sting. Which of the following is cited by NCERT as having a poison sting?

solution.explanation: NCERT: some cartilaginous fishes have electric organs (e.g. Torpedo) and some possess a poison sting (e.g. Trygon, the sting ray). Scoliodon is the dog fish, Pristis the saw fish and Carcharodon the great white shark.
solution.why_others_wrong: Scoliodon (dog fish), Pristis (saw fish) and Carcharodon (great white shark) are cartilaginous fishes, but NCERT does not cite them for a poison sting.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Animal Kingdom', class Chondrichthyes
solution.final_answer: Option B: Trygon

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Branchiostoma, commonly called Amphioxus or lancelet, is placed in the subphylum:

solution.explanation: NCERT gives Branchiostoma (Amphioxus or Lancelet) as the example of Cephalochordata, in which the notochord extends from head to tail. Ascidia, Salpa and Doliolum are urochordates.
solution.why_others_wrong: Urochordates are Ascidia, Salpa and Doliolum; Branchiostoma has no vertebral column, so it is not a vertebrate; Hemichordata is now a separate non-chordate phylum (Balanoglossus, Saccoglossus).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Animal Kingdom', phylum Chordata
solution.final_answer: Option C: Cephalochordata

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which phylum does NCERT describe as the second largest animal phylum?

solution.explanation: NCERT opens its description of phylum Mollusca by calling it the second largest animal phylum. Arthropoda is the largest phylum, containing over two-thirds of all named species.
solution.why_others_wrong: Arthropoda is the largest phylum, not the second largest; NCERT does not rank Annelida or Chordata in this way.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Animal Kingdom', phylum Mollusca
solution.final_answer: Option D: Mollusca

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Respiration by gills, by lungs and through the skin is described by NCERT for members of class:

solution.explanation: NCERT: in amphibians, respiration is by gills, lungs and through the skin. Their skin is moist and without scales. Reptiles and birds respire by lungs, and bony fishes respire by gills.
solution.why_others_wrong: Reptiles have dry, cornified skin and respire by lungs; birds respire by lungs supplemented by air sacs; bony fishes respire by gills.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Animal Kingdom', class Amphibia
solution.final_answer: Option B: Amphibia

Capture of prey with stinging cells
Food gathering, respiratory exchange and removal of waste

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In sponges, digestion is intracellular.
Reason (R): Sponges have a complete alimentary canal with a separate mouth and anus.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT states that digestion in sponges is intracellular, so A is true. Sponges show only the cellular level of organisation; their cells are loose aggregates and they have a water canal system, not an alimentary canal with a mouth and an anus. R is false.
steps: R → false (no alimentary canal; cellular level of organisation)
solution.why_others_wrong: A and B treat R as true; D calls the NCERT statement on intracellular digestion false.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Animal Kingdom', phylum Porifera
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements are correct?

(a) In birds, the endoskeleton is fully ossified (bony).
(b) The skin of mammals is unique in possessing hair.

solution.concept: Features of Aves, Mammalia and Reptilia
solution.explanation: NCERT: in birds the endoskeleton is fully ossified (bones) and they are warm-blooded (homoiothermous). Mammals are unique in possessing hair on the skin, and their most unique characteristic is the presence of mammary glands. Reptiles have dry, cornified skin with epidermal scales or scutes.
steps: (e) false – reptilian skin is dry and cornified, with scales
solution.why_others_wrong: Any option containing (d) or (e) is wrong; B also leaves out the true statement (a).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Animal Kingdom', classes Reptilia, Aves and Mammalia
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: An animal has dry, cornified skin with epidermal scales, two pairs of limbs and a tympanum that represents the ear. It is cold-blooded, fertilisation is internal and development is direct. To which class does it belong?

solution.concept: Identifying a vertebrate class from combined features
solution.explanation: NCERT (Reptilia): the body is covered by dry, cornified skin with epidermal scales or scutes; the tympanum represents the ear; limbs, when present, are two pairs; they are poikilotherms; fertilisation is internal and they are oviparous with direct development.
steps: Dry cornified skin + scales → not Amphibia (moist skin, no scales)
Scales, tympanum as ear, direct development → Reptilia
solution.why_others_wrong: Amphibians have moist skin without scales and indirect development; birds and mammals are warm-blooded, and mammals have external ears (pinnae).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Animal Kingdom', class Reptilia
solution.final_answer: Option A: Reptilia

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about phylum Chordata are correct?

(a) A pharynx perforated by gill slits is present in chordates and absent in non-chordates.

solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Animal Kingdom', phylum Chordata

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

steps: Name Cnidaria comes from cnidoblasts → R explains A

solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Animal Kingdom', phylum Coelenterata (Cnidaria)

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which statement correctly describes the life history of cyclostomes as given in NCERT?

They are marine but migrate to fresh water for spawning; after spawning, within a few days, they die, and their larvae, after metamorphosis, return to the ocean
They are marine and spawn in the sea; their larvae migrate to fresh water and remain there throughout life

Die within a few days of spawning
Larvae metamorphose and return to the ocean

Statement I: Ctenophores, commonly known as sea walnuts or comb jellies, show both extracellular and intracellular digestion.
Statement II: In ctenophores, locomotion is brought about by cnidoblasts present on the tentacles and body.

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: in ctenophores (sea walnuts or comb jellies) digestion is both extracellular and intracellular. The body bears eight external rows of ciliated comb plates, which help in locomotion. Cnidoblasts (stinging cells) are the feature of cnidarians (coelenterates), not of ctenophores, so Statement II is false.
steps: Statement II → false (comb plates, not cnidoblasts, help in locomotion)
solution.why_others_wrong: A and D give ctenophores the cnidoblasts of cnidarians and miss the comb plates; B rejects the true NCERT description of their digestion.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Animal Kingdom', phylum Ctenophora
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: The epithelium of the proximal convoluted tubule (PCT) of the nephron is cuboidal. According to NCERT, its free surface bears:

solution.explanation: NCERT: cuboidal epithelium is commonly found in the ducts of glands and the tubular parts of nephrons, and its main functions are secretion and absorption. The epithelium of the proximal convoluted tubule (PCT) of the nephron in the kidney has microvilli.
solution.why_others_wrong: Cilia are borne by ciliated epithelium (bronchioles, fallopian tubes); flagella are not described for this epithelium; several cell layers describe compound epithelium.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Structural Organisation in Animals', animal tissues: epithelial tissue
solution.final_answer: Option B: Microvilli

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: In connective tissues (other than blood), the cells secrete fibres of the structural proteins collagen or elastin. According to NCERT, these fibres provide the tissue with:

options.text: The ability to contract on stimulation
A free surface facing a body fluid

solution.explanation: NCERT: in all connective tissues except blood, the cells secrete fibres of structural proteins called collagen or elastin. The fibres provide strength, elasticity and flexibility to the tissue.
steps: Collagen/elastin fibres → strength, elasticity and flexibility
solution.why_others_wrong: Conducting impulses is a property of neural tissue, contraction of muscle tissue, and a free surface is a feature of epithelial tissue.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Structural Organisation in Animals', animal tissues: connective tissue
solution.final_answer: Option C: Strength, elasticity and flexibility

questions.question_text: Which sequence correctly traces the path of the glomerular filtrate in a human nephron until it leaves the kidney?

options.text: Bowman's capsule → DCT → Henle's loop → PCT → collecting duct → renal pelvis

Bowman's capsule → Henle's loop → PCT → DCT → renal pelvis → collecting duct
Bowman's capsule → PCT → Henle's loop → DCT → collecting duct → renal pelvis

solution.explanation: NCERT: the renal tubule begins with the double-walled Bowman's capsule, continues as the highly coiled PCT, then the hairpin-shaped Henle's loop (descending and ascending limbs), which continues as the highly coiled DCT. The DCTs of many nephrons open into a straight collecting duct; many collecting ducts converge and open into the renal pelvis through the medullary pyramids in the calyces.
steps: Bowman's capsule → PCT → Henle's loop → DCT → collecting duct → renal pelvis

Brush border of the proximal convoluted tubule

solution.explanation: NCERT: blood is filtered through three layers – the endothelium of the glomerular blood vessels, the epithelium of Bowman's capsule (with podocytes leaving filtration slits) and a basement membrane between them. The filtration is so fine that almost all constituents of plasma except the proteins pass into the lumen of Bowman's capsule. Proteins in the filtrate point to damage of this barrier, which lies before the tubule.
steps: Proteins are normally held back at filtration
Protein in the filtrate → filtration membrane damaged

solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Excretory Products and their Elimination', urine formation (glomerular filtration)

A healthy person drinks a large volume of water in a short time. Which of the following responses are expected?

(a) The rise in body fluid volume switches off the osmoreceptors.
(b) Release of ADH from the neurohypophysis is suppressed.
(c) Less water is reabsorbed from the latter parts of the tubule, so a larger volume of dilute urine is formed.
(d) The JG cells release more renin.
(e) Aldosterone secretion rises and more Na⁺ is reabsorbed from the distal parts of the tubule.

solution.concept: Regulation by ADH in excess water intake
solution.explanation: NCERT: osmoreceptors respond to changes in blood volume, body fluid volume and ionic concentration. An increase in body fluid volume can switch off the osmoreceptors and suppress ADH release, completing the feedback. ADH normally facilitates water reabsorption from the latter parts of the tubule, so with less ADH more dilute urine is passed. Renin and aldosterone respond to a fall in glomerular blood flow or GFR, which is not the situation here.
steps: (d) false – renin is released when GFR falls
(e) false – not triggered by excess water
solution.why_others_wrong: A includes (d); B includes (d) and (e); C omits the first step (a) of the response.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Excretory Products and their Elimination', regulation of kidney function

questions.question_text: The GFR of a healthy person is 125 mL per minute. Each kidney has nearly one million nephrons; take exactly 10⁶ nephrons per kidney and assume all nephrons filter equally. About how much filtrate does one nephron form per minute? (1 mL = 10⁶ nL)

solution.explanation: NCERT: GFR in a healthy individual is approximately 125 mL per minute, and each kidney has nearly one million nephrons. Two kidneys → 2 × 10⁶ nephrons. Filtrate per nephron = 125 mL ÷ (2 × 10⁶) = 125 × 10⁶ nL ÷ (2 × 10⁶) = 62.5 nL per minute.
solution.why_others_wrong: 125 nL counts the nephrons of only one kidney; 6.25 nL is a slip of a power of ten; 62.5 µL confuses nanolitres with microlitres (1000 times too large).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Excretory Products and their Elimination', human excretory system; urine formation
solution.final_answer: Option C: 62.5 nL

questions.question_text:
After a severe loss of blood, a person's blood pressure and GFR fall. Which of the following responses are expected according to the regulatory mechanisms described in NCERT?

(a) The JG cells release renin.
(b) Angiotensin II constricts blood vessels, raising the glomerular blood pressure and thereby the GFR.
(c) Aldosterone causes reabsorption of Na⁺ and water from the distal parts of the tubule.
(d) ANF release increases and causes vasodilation.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Responses to a fall in blood pressure
solution.explanation: NCERT: a fall in glomerular blood flow, glomerular blood pressure or GFR activates the JG cells to release renin, which converts angiotensinogen to angiotensin I and II. Angiotensin II, a powerful vasoconstrictor, raises the glomerular blood pressure and GFR, and activates the adrenal cortex to release aldosterone, which causes reabsorption of Na⁺ and water from the distal tubule, raising BP and GFR. ANF is released when blood flow to the atria increases and causes vasodilation – the opposite of what is needed after blood loss.
steps: (d) false – ANF is a check on this mechanism, released on increased atrial blood flow
solution.why_others_wrong: A, C and D include (d); C also leaves out (b) and (c).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Excretory Products and their Elimination', regulation of kidney function
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b) and (c) only

Henle's loop and the vasa recta

The flow in their two limbs is counter-current, which maintains an increasing osmolarity towards the inner medulla (300 to about 1200 mOsmol L⁻¹); this gradient allows water to be reabsorbed from the collecting tubule to concentrate the filtrate.

Gradient is built and kept by Henle's loop and vasa recta

solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Excretory Products and their Elimination', mechanism of concentration of the filtrate

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: In a juxtamedullary nephron, how does the filtrate at the hairpin bend of Henle's loop (deep in the medulla) compare with the filtrate that has just passed up the ascending limb?

options.text: Filtrate at the bend is dilute, and filtrate after the ascending limb is more concentrated
Filtrate after the ascending limb is still more concentrated than at the bend
Filtrate at the bend is highly concentrated, and it gets diluted as it passes up the ascending limb

solution.concept: Changes in the filtrate along Henle's loop
solution.explanation: NCERT: the descending limb is permeable to water but almost impermeable to electrolytes, so the filtrate gets concentrated as it moves down towards the inner medulla, where the interstitium reaches about 1200 mOsmol L⁻¹. The ascending limb is impermeable to water but allows transport of electrolytes to the medullary fluid, so the concentrated filtrate gets diluted as it moves up.
steps: Descending limb: water leaves → filtrate concentrated at the bend
Ascending limb: electrolytes leave, water cannot → filtrate diluted
solution.why_others_wrong: A ignores the medullary gradient; B reverses the changes; C forgets that the ascending limb removes electrolytes without water.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Excretory Products and their Elimination', function of the tubules; mechanism of concentration of the filtrate
solution.final_answer: Option D: Filtrate at the bend is highly concentrated, and it gets diluted as it passes up the ascending limb

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which sequence correctly describes transmission of an impulse across a chemical synapse?

options.text: Neurotransmitters bind receptors on the pre-synaptic membrane → synaptic vesicles fuse with the post-synaptic membrane → new potential in the pre-synaptic neuron
Ion channels open on the post-synaptic membrane → impulse arrives at the axon terminal → synaptic vesicles release neurotransmitters
Electrical current flows directly from the pre-synaptic to the post-synaptic membrane → neurotransmitters are released afterwards

Impulse arrives at the axon terminal → synaptic vesicles move to and fuse with the plasma membrane → neurotransmitters are released into the synaptic cleft → they bind specific receptors on the post-synaptic membrane → ion channels open and a new potential may be generated

solution.explanation: NCERT: when an impulse arrives at the axon terminal, it stimulates the movement of synaptic vesicles towards the membrane, where they fuse with the plasma membrane and release their neurotransmitters into the synaptic cleft. The neurotransmitters bind to specific receptors on the post-synaptic membrane; this opens ion channels, allowing the entry of ions which can generate a new potential in the post-synaptic neuron.
steps: Arrival of impulse → vesicles fuse → release into cleft → binding to post-synaptic receptors → ion channels open → new potential
solution.why_others_wrong: A places receptors on the pre-synaptic side; B starts with channel opening before the impulse arrives; C describes an electrical synapse.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Neural Control and Coordination', transmission of impulses
solution.final_answer: Option D: Impulse arrives at the axon terminal → synaptic vesicles move to and fuse with the plasma membrane → neurotransmitters are released into the synaptic cleft → they bind specific receptors on the post-synaptic membrane → ion channels open and a new potential may be generated

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
A drug prevents the axonal membrane from becoming permeable to Na⁺ when it is stimulated, but does not affect the resting membrane. Which of the following would be expected?

(a) The resting potential of the axon can still exist.
(b) On stimulation, the rapid influx of Na⁺ cannot occur.
(c) The inner surface at the stimulated site does not become positively charged, so no action potential arises.
(d) The membrane at the stimulated site undergoes a reversal of polarity as usual.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Role of Na⁺ influx in the action potential
solution.explanation: NCERT: the resting potential depends on the ionic gradients maintained by the sodium–potassium pump and on the resting membrane being more permeable to K⁺ and nearly impermeable to Na⁺, so it is unaffected. When a stimulus is applied, the membrane normally becomes freely permeable to Na⁺, leading to a rapid influx of Na⁺ and a reversal of polarity (inner surface positive) – the action potential. Without that rise in Na⁺ permeability, no influx, no reversal and no action potential occur.
solution.why_others_wrong: A and C include (d); D leaves out the true statements (a) and (b).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Neural Control and Coordination', generation and conduction of nerve impulse
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b) and (c) only

Impulses from the limb reach the CNS, but regulatory impulses from the CNS cannot reach the limb
Both kinds of impulses pass normally, because the PNS has only one type of fibre
Impulses from the limb can no longer reach the CNS, but regulatory impulses from the CNS can still reach the limb

solution.explanation: NCERT: the nerve fibres of the PNS are of two types – afferent fibres transmit impulses from tissues and organs to the CNS, and efferent fibres transmit regulatory impulses from the CNS to the concerned peripheral tissues and organs. Losing only the afferent fibres blocks the limb-to-CNS route while the CNS-to-limb route remains.
solution.why_others_wrong: A also blocks the intact efferent route; B reverses the roles of afferent and efferent fibres; C ignores that the PNS has two kinds of fibres.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Neural Control and Coordination', human neural system
solution.final_answer: Option D: Impulses from the limb can no longer reach the CNS, but regulatory impulses from the CNS can still reach the limb

A toxin prevents synaptic vesicles from fusing with the pre-synaptic membrane at chemical synapses only. Which of the following would be expected?

(b) No new potential is generated in the post-synaptic neuron across these synapses.
(c) The pre-synaptic neuron itself loses its resting potential.
(d) Transmission at electrical synapses, where current flows directly from one neuron into the other, continues.

solution.explanation: NCERT: at a chemical synapse, the arriving impulse makes synaptic vesicles fuse with the plasma membrane and release neurotransmitters into the cleft; these bind post-synaptic receptors, open ion channels and can generate a new potential. If fusion fails, nothing is released and no post-synaptic potential arises. The pre-synaptic neuron's own resting potential depends on its ionic gradients, not on transmitter release. At electrical synapses, current flows directly from one neuron into the other, without neurotransmitters.
steps: (c) false – the resting potential is unaffected
solution.why_others_wrong: A leaves out (d); B and D include (c), and D also leaves out (a).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Neural Control and Coordination', transmission of impulses
solution.final_answer: Option C: (a), (b) and (d) only
